sensitive_conditions: Global 1/L-cocoercivity is stronger than monotonicity plus L-Lipschitz continuity.

complexity_scope.hidden_constants: The displayed residual inequality has explicit constant 1; no hidden residual-bound constants. Oracle cost is counted separately from vector arithmetic.

complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Last iterate u_k; operator residual norm ||F(u_k)||.
complexity_scope.regime: All k>=1, global cocoercivity and nonempty zero set; known positive L.
complexity_scope.resource: Producing u_k from u0 takes k evaluations F(u0),...,F(u_{k-1}). Evaluating its residual additionally requires F(u_k), hence k+1 evaluations including certification; cached residual values at earlier iterates can be reused for updates. Vector arithmetic is charged separately: O(d) per update in Euclidean coordinates; a norm test also costs O(d). No projection or resolvent calls are used.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Only the explicitly defined deterministic known-L Halpern sequence. This is an upper bound, with no lower-bound claim or coverage of unrestricted algorithms.

proofs.source_argument: Complete paraphrase of the source argument, specialized to its explicitly stated known-L parameters; this is not a new local Theorem. Write f_j=F(u_j), lambda_j=1/(j+1), A_j=j(j+1)/2, and C_j=||f_j||²/L-<f_j,u0-u_j>/j for j>=1. The first update is u1=u0-f0/L. Cocoercivity at (u1,u0) gives -<f1-f0,f0> >= ||f1-f0||², hence ||f1||² <= <f1,f0>. Consequently C1=(||f1||²-<f1,f0>)/L<=0. For j>=1 put a=lambda_{j+1}=1/(j+2) and delta=u_{j+1}-u_j. Consecutive-iterate cocoercivity, expanded, gives ||f_{j+1}||²/L <= <f_{j+1},delta+2f_j/L>-<f_j,delta>-||f_j||²/L. In the original p.16 display the final contribution is written as -<f_j,delta+f_j/L>; expanding this inner product gives -<f_j,delta>-||f_j||²/L. This is the original formula's ordinary algebraic expansion, with no source defect or transcription correction asserted. The update implies delta=a/(1-a)(u0-u_{j+1})-2f_j/L and also delta=a(u0-u_j)-2(1-a)f_j/L. Substitution yields C_{j+1} <= (1-2a)||f_j||²/L-a<f_j,u0-u_j>. Since A_{j+1}(1-2a)=A_j and A_{j+1}a=A_j/j, multiplication gives A_{j+1}C_{j+1}<=A_jC_j. Thus C_k<=0 for every k>=1. Monotonicity and F(u*)=0 give <f_k,u*-u_k><=0. Therefore ||f_k||² <= (L/k)<f_k,u0-u_k> <= (L/k)<f_k,u0-u*> <= (L/k)||f_k||||u0-u*||. If f_k=0 the result is immediate; otherwise divide by ||f_k||. All identities above follow the source Proofs on pp.15–16 with the p.6 parameter substitution.

assumptions: The domain is unconstrained, U=E; all updates use the exact value of F and the stated fixed L.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let E be a real d-dimensional inner-product space with its induced norm, F:E→E, and Z={u∈E:F(u)=0}. Let u0∈E and let u*∈Z minimize ||u0-u*||. Define u_{j+1}=u0/(j+2)+(j+1)/(j+2)[u_j-(2/L)F(u_j)] for every integer j>=0.
statement.parameter_domains: d is a positive integer; L∈(0,∞); u0∈E; k∈{1,2,...}.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such finite-dimensional E, F, L and initial point u0, the deterministic sequence satisfies the conclusion simultaneously for every integer k>=1; no probabilistic qualification.
